purpose: Locked exact known-answer test vectors for the dimensional-analysis / unit-conversion axis of the known-answer benchmark. Every expected value is fixed by an exact rational defining constant published in a primary authority (NIST SP 811 2008; NIST HB 44 App C; BIPM SI; ASTM D2697; EPA Method 24). No empirical fit; no candidate performance claim. AUDIT_ONLY.
scope: solvent-borne two-part epoxy-amine marine anti-corrosion coating formulation arithmetic

exact_defining_constants.Imperial_gallon_L: 4.54609 (exact, for negative-control trap only; NOT used in US coating specs)

tolerance_policy: Each positive vector pins the expected value to the stated decimal places; the independent verifier re-derives the value from the exact rational defining constants and PASSES iff round(exact_rational, decimals) equals the pinned expected. Float arithmetic is not used in the gate.

positive_vectors.primary_source: NIST SP 811 (2008) Appendix B.8, entry 'pound per gallon (U.S. liquid) -> gram per cubic centimeter' reciprocal = 8.345 404 E+00
positive_vectors.relevance: coating component density is quoted lb/gal on US TDS and g/mL in SI; the two MIL-DTL-24441 F-160 controls in this module are gated in lb/gal
regulatory VOC limits for marine coatings are set in both g/L and lb/gal
2.8 lb/gal is a common high-solids marine-primer VOC ceiling
DFT specs are quoted in mils (US) and microns (SI)
5 mil is a typical single-coat epoxy DFT

positive_vectors.primary_source: The '1604 rule': 1 US gal = 231 in^3 exactly, spread to 0.001 in => 231/0.001 in^2 = 231000 in^2 = 231000/144 ft^2
positive_vectors.relevance: coverage math underlies practical spreading-rate and cost-per-area estimates

positive_vectors.primary_source: Exact: 1 L = 1000 cm^3 spread to 1e-4 cm => 1000/1e-4 cm^2 = 1e7 cm^2 = 1000 m^2

positive_vectors.relevance: cross-consistency of the two coverage constants; catches a US<->SI coverage-rule swap
cure-kinetics and pot-life arithmetic use absolute temperature; the module ARITH controls are anchored at 25 C
batch-mass unit base for density conversions

positive_vectors.primary_source: NIST HB 44: 1 US gal = 231 in^3 = 3.785411784 L exact

fail_closed_hostile_vectors.trap: 8.33 lb/gal is the density of WATER, routinely mis-applied as the g/mL->lb/gal conversion factor. It is NOT the conversion constant (8.345404). A verifier that accepts 8.33 has a unit regression.
fail_closed_hostile_vectors.must_flag_reason: abs(8.33 - 8.345404) = 0.015404 lb/gal exceeds the 0.5 ulp at 6 decimals

fail_closed_hostile_vectors.trap: Using the Imperial (UK) gallon 4.54609 L instead of the US gallon 3.785411784 L yields 10.0224 lb/gal. US marine coating specs (MIL-DTL-24441, ASTM) use the US gallon.
Treating 1 mil as 1 mm (1000 um) instead of 25.4 um is a 39.37x thickness error that silently 40x-inflates coverage.
